summary: Snapshot 2026-10-14. The plague lane is over; every candidate below sits inside the GLP-1 focus. Four things are moving at once. (1) An Oct 13 CBS News investigation found the FDA received two death reports tied to products sold as 'retatrutide' ('Reta'). The details are unverified and it's not clear the products contained the real drug. Newsweek, Gizmodo, MedPage and NewsNation picked it up within 24 h. (2) Lilly's TRIUMPH-2 results for retatrutide in type 2 diabetes (Lancet/EASD): 20.8% vs 4.0% on placebo at 80 weeks, with a filing planned for Q1 2027. Search queries like 'what is retatrutide / when available' are spiking. Together (1) and (2) are our best opportunity, because they match our proven myth-bust format (56) and our named-next-gen-drug format. (3) A pills lane: Lilly reported an indirect comparison (Sep 29) where Foundayo (orforglipron, FDA-approved Apr 1, 2026) beat oral semaglutide 25 mg in type 2 diabetes. The Wegovy pill passed 100k prescriptions a month and got EU approval in July. (4) Practical 'what does it do to my body' questions: the EADV nail and hair study (39% vs 9% nail detachment, with heavy caveats), a pilot RCT on keeping weight off after stopping (usual care regained an estimated 10.75% vs about 3.6% with meals or an app), and the USA Today syndicated piece 'mistake specialists see' (not eating enough or too little protein), which feeds our muscle winner. Smaller hooks: the international pregnancy consensus, heart-failure benefit, tirzepatide and diabetic eye disease, surgery on GLP-1s, and the semaglutide addiction trials. TOGETHER-PsO and the Wegovy pill uptake story are fading (lower momentum across snapshots). Status lines to carry: retatrutide is investigational as of Oct 2026 (Lilly plans to file Q1 2027); Foundayo was FDA-approved Apr 1, 2026; the Wegovy pill was approved Dec 22, 2025 (US) and July 2026 (EU); Wegovy HD 7.2 mg was approved in March 2026. Two leads could not be verified directly: the Pittsburgh 1,200-person addiction trial and the FDA warning to online sellers of semaglutide marketed under Indian drugmakers' brands. Scripts on these must check the primary source first.

candidates.topic: Bootleg 'Reta': 2 death reports to FDA linked to online products sold as retatrutide (CBS News, Oct 13, 2026). Unverified, and it's unclear what was actually in the vials
candidates.angle: Myth-bust in our proven format: 'Online "Reta" isn't the trial drug.' Retatrutide is investigational as of Oct 2026, and no pharmacy can legally sell it. Credit the 2 reports to the FDA via CBS News, keep the caveat 'details unverified; unclear whether patients actually took retatrutide', and add the poison-center rise. Point to a prescriber and approved options. Never name a seller or say how to buy.
candidates.why_now: CBS broke the documents Oct 13. Newsweek, Gizmodo, MedPage, NewsNation and Medical Daily followed within 24 h, and 'what is Reta' searches are surging. It matches our 56-view 'online retatrutide' Short pattern, plus a fresh news hook.

evidence.signal: Investigation: 2 death reports to FDA tied to products claiming to be retatrutide
Details unverified; unclear whether patients took real retatrutide (July: 41-year-old woman; September: 49-year-old)

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 (type 2 diabetes plus overweight/obesity): Lilly reported 20.8% weight loss on 12 mg vs 4.0% on placebo at 80 weeks (Lancet/EASD); FDA filing planned Q1 2027
candidates.angle: 'What is retatrutide, and when could it be available?' Explain the triple-hormone mechanism (GIP, GLP-1, glucagon), give one number with its comparator and population, and add the A1C result (up to 1.6 points lower). Say clearly that it's investigational as of Oct 2026 and that it was not compared head-to-head with tirzepatide. Pairs naturally with the bootleg warning: 'the real drug is coming through trials, not the internet.'
candidates.why_now: Phase 3 results in type 2 diabetes were just published in the Lancet. Motley Fool and Stocktwits say retatrutide matters more than Lilly's Oct 29 earnings, and SEO farms are mass-publishing 'retatrutide' query pages, a sign of heavy search demand.

evidence.signal: Up to 20.8% (12 mg) vs 4.0% placebo at 80 wk in adults with T2D and obesity/overweight
TRIUMPH-2 detailed results; BLA planned Q1 2027
Lilly to seek FDA approval with new data

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) vs oral semaglutide (Wegovy pill): Lilly's indirect comparison in type 2 diabetes (1.5% more weight loss, 0.3 more A1C reduction at 52 weeks) plus the ACHIEVE-3 head-to-head
candidates.angle: 'Which GLP-1 pill did better: orforglipron or oral semaglutide?' Name both sides, give one number, and note that the indirect comparison isn't a head-to-head trial. ACHIEVE-3 is the direct one, versus oral semaglutide 7/14 mg in type 2 diabetes. Explain why one pill has no food or water rules (non-peptide) and the other does. Date both approvals. This builds on our semaglutide pill Short (52 Instagram reach).
candidates.why_now: Stocktwits and others reported 'Foundayo beats Novo's oral semaglutide' on Oct 14. Pill search interest is already proven ('what is the new weight loss pill called'). Approved pills now compete in both the US and the EU.

evidence.signal: Foundayo superior A1C and weight in 3 pivotal T2D trials; ACHIEVE-3 vs oral semaglutide
Indirect comparison: 1.5% more weight loss and 0.3 points more A1C vs oral semaglutide 25 mg; not a direct comparison
FDA approved orforglipron for obesity on Apr 1, 2026

candidates.topic: GLP-1 and your nails and hair: EADV 2026 study found 39% of GLP-1 users reported nail detachment vs 9% of non-users (575 users vs 1,329 controls)
candidates.angle: 'Does a GLP-1 affect your nails?' A calm 'what does it do to my body' answer: it's linked, not proven to cause. About half the users reported nail problems before treatment, and the change may relate to rapid weight loss and eating less. The helpful turn: protein and overall nutrition matter, and new nail or hair changes are worth raising with your prescriber. No emoji in the hook.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily (Oct 11) and Men's Journal (Oct 12) picked it up after the EADV presentation and the Medical Economics/Advisory coverage. Consumer pickup is now ramping, and it's a visual, relatable side-effect question.

evidence.signal: Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem
GLP-1 users report more nail detachment and hair loss than non-users
Caveat: may be indirect, from rapid weight loss and lower intake

candidates.topic: Keeping weight off after stopping a GLP-1: pilot RCT (Obes Sci Pract) found usual care regained an estimated 10.75% over 4 months vs 3.58% with medically tailored meals and 3.60% with a wellness app
candidates.angle: 'What happens when you stop a GLP-1, and what might slow the regain?' Use STEP 1 extension and SURMOUNT-4 for context, then this small pilot: both support groups still regained some weight. It's a pilot, and it gives no stopping advice. Close with 'plan any change with your prescriber.'
keywords: what happens when you stop ozempic
how to keep weight off after wegovy
candidates.why_now: In the last 24 h, Medical News Today, ABC27 and Business Insider ('not a free lunch') all ran on stopping and maintenance. It's one of our double-down topics, with a fresh RCT hook.

evidence.signal: Pilot RCT results: 10.75% vs ~3.6% regain over 4 months

Explain the SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy (obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, without diabetes), give the guideline-style protein and strength habits as 'recommended', and keep the kidney caveat and 'start gently'.

Never name a seller, price or route. Close with 'talk to your doctor or prescriber' and approved, prescribed options. Script must pull the FDA warning letter itself before writing.

candidates.topic: Planning a pregnancy on a GLP-1? The first international consensus (Lancet Obstet Gynaecol Womens Health, Sep 29, 2026), plus new data on GLP-1s and fertility and PCOS
candidates.angle: A calm explainer of the consensus: don't deliberately continue these medicines in pregnancy, and if exposure happens early, current data show no increase in birth defects (more than 42,000 exposed women). Note the open questions (the miscarriage data are mixed), and that oral contraceptives may interact with tirzepatide. Say 'plan with your prescriber'. No stopping instructions.
candidates.why_now: ABC News and ABC13 ran a GLP-1 fertility feature Oct 14. Medscape covered the consensus Oct 14, and the JCEM PCOS preconception study came out Oct 10. 'Ozempic babies' is a recurring viral question.

evidence.signal: Consensus: incretin drugs should not be deliberately continued in pregnancy
